messages.author: b01d5d02b1ad8349
messages.subject: Multiple Group Error Message
parts:
Hello,

Me and my colleague are trying to run a multiple group model (you may have seen these variables before). We are using code given to us by Todd Little at stats camp. We thought we adapted the code correctly; however, we keep getting an error:

Error in lavaanify(model = FLAT, meanstructure = lavaanOptions$meanstructure,  : 
  lavaan ERROR: wrong number of arguments in modifier (V1,V1) of element w3strain~~w3strain

Are you able to see where we may have gone wrong? Here is the code for our null model:

################################################################################
## Longitudinal 4-group CFA -- Null model
################################################################################

null.model <- '

## no change in variances over time, no covariances
     w3strain ~~ c(V1, V1)*w3strain
     w4strain ~~ c(V2, V2)*w4strain
     w3alc1 ~~ c(V3, V3)*w3alc1
     w4alc1 ~~ c(V4, V4)*w4alc1
     w3access ~~ c(V1, V1)*w3access
     w4ladder ~~ c(V2, V2)*w4ladder
     w3alc2 ~~ c(V3, V3)*w3alc2
     w4alc2 ~~ c(V4, V4)*w4alc2
     w3income ~~ c(V1, V1)*w3income
     w4income ~~ c(V2, V2)*w4income
     w3ex1 ~~ c(V3, V3)*w3ex1
     w4ex1 ~~ c(V4, V4)*w4ex1
     w3ex2 ~~ c(V3, V3)*w3ex2
     w4ex2 ~~ c(V4, V4)*w4ex2

## no change in means over time
     w3strain ~ c(T1, T1)*1
     w4strain ~ c(T2, T2)*1
     w3alc1 ~ c(T3, T3)*1
     w4alc1 ~ c(T4, T4)*1
     w3access ~ c(T1, T1)*1
     w4ladder ~ c(T2, T2)*1
     w3alc2 ~ c(T3, T3)*1
     w4alc2 ~ c(T4, T4)*1
     w3income ~ c(T1, T1)*1
     w4income ~ c(T2, T2)*1
     w3ex1 ~ c(T3, T3)*1
     w4ex1 ~ c(T4, T4)*1
     w3ex2 ~ c(T3, T3)*1
     w4ex2 ~ c(T4, T4)*1
'

null.fit <- lavaan(null.model, data=niaaagroup, orthogonal=T, group="livecollege")

summary(null.fit, standardized=T, fit.measures=T)

Thank you in advance for any assistance you can provide!

messages.author: 5d4f9e7f97c21008
messages.subject: Re: Multiple Group Error Message
parts:
Each element in the list references one group. So:

 w3strain ~~ c(V1, V1)*w3strain
Equates the covariance across two groups

 w3strain ~~ c(V1, V1, V1)*w3strain
Would equate the covariance across three groups

and...

 w3strain ~~ c(V1, V1, V1, V1)*w3strain
Would equate the covariance across four groups
